item.title: Data Science Machine Learning
item.description:
The Problem
This repository addresses the gap between learning Python data science libraries and applying them to real-world business problems. Most tutorials stop at isolated library examples, and most project repos lack the breadth to show how NumPy, Pandas, visualization, and machine learning fit together in actual workflows. This repo attempts to bridge that by pairing library tutorials with applied projects across finance, insurance, and e-commerce.

Doing this manually requires API plumbing, data cleaning, and ad‑hoc analysis notebooks, which slows reporting cycles and introduces inconsistency.

item.title: string search server
item.description:
High-performance TCP string-search server in Python: multiple search algorithm implementations, SSL auth, concurrent connections, and a benchmark harness.
This Python project caught my attention for its practical approach to solving real developer problems. The codebase offers patterns worth studying for anyone working in this space.

item.title: bare lm
item.description:
The Problem
Training small neural networks in C typically means either hand-writing backpropagation for each model or pulling in a heavyweight framework. bare-lm addresses that gap with a minimal autograd engine that tracks the computation graph, computes gradients, and runs SGD—all in C with no Python dependency.

item.title: WiFiDuck
item.description:
The Problem Security trainers and penetration‑test teams need a low‑cost, easily programmable BadUSB that can be re‑programmed on‑the‑fly without opening the device or flashing a new binary each time. Existing solutions require SD cards or recompilation, which slows iteration and makes classroom demos cumbersome.

item.title: open kritt
item.description:
The Problem
Security researchers and developers need to find code vulnerabilities at scale, but pointing a single model at an entire repository produces noisy, unverified results. open·kritt addresses this by breaking research into focused, parallelizable tasks, then de-duplicating and ranking findings with configurable validation. It is built for teams that need control over prompts, model providers, and workflow orchestration rather than opaque, black-box scanning.

item.title: robotics toolbox python
item.description:
The Problem
Robotics research and education requires significant boilerplate for kinematics, dynamics, and visualization. Researchers often hand-roll transformation math, inverse kinematics solvers, and robot model loaders, which leads to inconsistent results and wasted effort. This toolbox consolidates those primitives into one Python package.

item.title: tuios
item.description:
The Problem Developers who need to run multiple interactive shells inside a single terminal often resort to tmux or screen. Those tools lack modern UI features such as mouse‑driven pane resizing, native graphics (kitty/sixel), and a modal, vim‑like command palette, forcing users to maintain separate scripts for layout automation.

item.title: TraceAnything
item.description:
The Problem
Videos are typically processed as sequences of independent frames or as static 3D reconstructions, which loses temporal continuity. Tracking arbitrary points across a video—whether for editing, 3D reconstruction, or scene understanding—requires either expensive per-frame correspondence matching or specialized trackers that don't generalize well.
